signals.summary: Comprehensive taxonomy of AI fraud and abuse vectors: API abuse (token theft, proxy services, scraping), safety bypass monetization, platform fraud, downstream harm, data poisoning. Quantifies financial impact per vector category.
key_findings: API abuse rate benchmark: 0.8-3.2% of total API events in comparable systems
Safety bypass incidents: escalating over 24-month periods in observed cases
Coordinated abuse: detectable via graph analysis at cluster sizes >= 5 accounts
Regulatory lag: enforcement actions typically 60-120 days after internal detection

signals.topic: Sequential Probability Ratio Test (SPRT) for Abuse Detection
signals.source: Academic literature — Wald (1945) + applied ML adaptations
signals.summary: SPRT optimal sequential test for detecting Poisson rate changes. For abuse detection: null hypothesis = baseline rate λ₀, alternative = escalated rate λ₁. Stops as soon as evidence crosses decision boundary. More powerful than fixed-N tests for gradual escalation detection.
key_findings: SPRT detects safety_bypass escalation 3-4 months before threshold-based rules
Implementation: log-likelihood ratio cumulation; stop when LLR > A (accept H1) or < B (accept H0)
Type I error (false positive) and Type II error (false negative) are both controllable

signals.topic: Sample Ratio Mismatch (SRM) in A/B Testing
signals.source: Deng et al. (2021) — Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments
signals.summary: SRM occurs when observed treatment/control ratio differs from planned split. Even small SRM can invalidate experiment results. Detection: chi-squared test on sample counts vs. planned split. Root causes: experiment assignment bugs, bot traffic, selective attrition.
key_findings: SRM detection threshold: chi-squared p < 0.001 (stricter than standard 0.05)
Two injected SRM experiments in dataset: EXP-001 (p=2.3e-12), EXP-002 (p=0.003)
SRM resolution: pause experiment, diagnose assignment mechanism, rerun clean

signals.topic: Population Stability Index (PSI) for Pipeline Monitoring
signals.summary: PSI measures distribution shift between a reference population and current population. Standard thresholds: PSI < 0.10 = stable; 0.10-0.20 = minor shift (monitor); > 0.20 = major shift (investigate); > 0.50 = Diagnostic Agent L4 halt.
key_findings: PSI 0.10-0.20: L1 self-heal — hand to Healing Agent
PSI 0.20-0.50: L2 elevated — pause new work on pipeline
PSI > 0.50: L4 halt — immediate human escalation

signals.topic: EU AI Act — General Purpose AI (GPAI) provisions
signals.summary: GPAI provisions require downstream harm disclosure, systemic risk reporting, incident notification to national competent authorities. Enforcement from August 2025 for tier-1 GPAI providers. Fines up to €30M or 6% global turnover.
key_findings: Downstream harm monitoring is a regulatory requirement, not just an internal metric
Incident reporting timeline: 24-48 hours for high-impact events
Documentation requirements map directly to AIMS Mode B output format
